question: Why did scientists send animals to space before humans?
short_answer: Scientists launched animals into space to evaluate whether exposure to microgravity, cosmic radiation, severe g-forces, and launch vibrations would be fatal to biological organisms before risking human astronauts.
full_explanation: Early suborbital and orbital animal flights provided critical telemetry data on heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, and respiration during launch and weightlessness, validating life support system engineering.
